scale.who-5.3: More than half of the time
scale.who-5.2: Less than half of the time
instrument.phq-4.purpose: A one-minute read on how much low mood and worry are weighing on you right now.
instrument.phq-4.about: The PHQ-4 combines the two best-validated ultra-short screens for depression (PHQ-2) and anxiety (GAD-2) into four questions. It is a screening tool, not a diagnosis: it tells us roughly how much pressure you are carrying so we can suggest a sensible starting point, and whether a slightly longer set of questions is worth your time. Scored 0–12. Free to use, no permission required (Kroenke et al., 2009).
instrument.phq-4.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?
instrument.phq-4.item.q1: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
instrument.phq-4.item.q2: Not being able to stop or control worrying
instrument.phq-4.item.q3: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
instrument.phq-9.purpose: A closer look at how low mood has been affecting your days.
instrument.phq-9.about: The PHQ-9 is the most widely used depression severity measure in primary care worldwide. It asks about nine areas over the last two weeks and produces a 0–27 score with published severity bands. It is a measure of severity, not a diagnosis — a high score is a reason to talk to someone, not a label. Public domain (Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams, 2001).
instrument.phq-9.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
instrument.phq-9.item.q1: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
instrument.phq-9.item.q3: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
instrument.phq-9.item.q4: Feeling tired or having little energy
instrument.phq-9.item.q6: Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
instrument.phq-9.item.q7: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
instrument.phq-9.item.q8: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed — or the opposite, being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
instrument.phq-9.item.q9: Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way
instrument.gad-7.purpose: A closer look at how much worry and tension you have been carrying.
instrument.gad-7.about: The GAD-7 is the standard brief measure of anxiety severity, validated across general anxiety, panic, social anxiety and PTSD. Seven questions about the last two weeks produce a 0–21 score with published bands. It measures how much anxiety is present, not which condition you have. Free to use, no permission required (Spitzer et al., 2006).
instrument.gad-7.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?
instrument.gad-7.item.q1: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
instrument.gad-7.item.q2: Not being able to stop or control worrying
instrument.gad-7.item.q3: Worrying too much about different things
instrument.gad-7.item.q5: Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
instrument.gad-7.item.q7: Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen
instrument.who-5.purpose: A gentle read on your general wellbeing — and a good one to repeat later to see change.
instrument.who-5.about: The WHO-5 asks about positive wellbeing rather than symptoms, which makes it a kinder entry point and an excellent way to track change over time. Five statements produce a 0–100 score; below 50 suggests low wellbeing worth looking at, below 28 suggests looking further. Free to use, source acknowledged (WHO Regional Office for Europe, 1998).
instrument.who-5.prompt: Please indicate for each of the five statements which is closest to how you have been feeling over the last two weeks.
instrument.who-5.item.q1: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits
instrument.who-5.item.q2: I have felt calm and relaxed
instrument.who-5.item.q3: I have felt active and vigorous
instrument.who-5.item.q4: I woke up feeling fresh and rested
instrument.who-5.item.q5: My daily life has been filled with things that interest me
instrument.audit-c.purpose: Three quick questions about drinking, so any suggestion we make takes it into account.
instrument.audit-c.about: The AUDIT-C is the three-item short form of the WHO's AUDIT. It does not diagnose anything and it is not a judgement — it simply tells us whether it would be useful to include substance-aware resources alongside whatever else we suggest. Scored 0–12. Free to use (WHO; Bush et al., 1998).
instrument.audit-c.prompt: Some questions about your use of alcohol.
instrument.audit-c.item.q1: How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?
instrument.audit-c.item.q2: How many standard drinks containing alcohol do you have on a typical day when you are drinking?
instrument.audit-c.item.q3: How often do you have six or more drinks on one occasion?
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.purpose: A short, optional check on whether a difficult past event is still affecting you.
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.about: The PC-PTSD-5 is a five-question screen developed for primary care. A positive screen does not mean you have PTSD — it means that talking to someone trained in trauma-informed care is likely to be more useful for you than a general referral. Public domain (US VA National Center for PTSD, Prins et al., 2016).
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.prompt: In the past month, have you...
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.gate: Sometimes things happen to people that are unusually or especially frightening, horrible, or traumatic. Have you ever experienced this kind of event?
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.item.q1: Had nightmares about the event(s) or thought about the event(s) when you did not want to?
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.item.q2: Tried hard not to think about the event(s) or went out of your way to avoid situations that reminded you of the event(s)?
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.item.q3: Been constantly on guard, watchful, or easily startled?
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.item.q4: Felt numb or detached from people, activities, or your surroundings?
instrument.pc-ptsd-5.item.q5: Felt guilty or unable to stop blaming yourself or others for the event(s) or any problems the event(s) may have caused?
band.phq-4.none: Nothing here stands out as pressing. That is worth knowing too.
band.phq-4.mild: There is some strain showing. It is early, and small steps tend to work well at this stage.
band.phq-4.moderate: You are carrying a noticeable amount right now. A few more questions will help point you somewhere useful.
band.phq-4.severe: This is a heavy load to be carrying. Let us find you something solid.
band.phq-9.none: Low mood does not seem to be weighing on you much at the moment.
band.phq-9.mild: Some low mood is showing up. Often this responds well to structured self-help and support.
band.phq-9.moderate: Low mood is taking up real space in your days. This is the point where guided support usually helps most.
band.phq-9.moderately-severe: This is a significant amount to be carrying, and it deserves proper professional attention.
band.phq-9.severe: You are carrying a great deal. Please do not try to hold this alone — support that matches this exists.
band.gad-7.none: Worry does not appear to be dominating things right now.
band.gad-7.mild: Some anxiety is present. Structured tools tend to work well early.
band.gad-7.moderate: Anxiety is taking real energy from you. Guided or structured support usually helps at this level.
band.gad-7.severe: Anxiety is at a level that deserves proper professional support.
band.who-5.very-low: Your wellbeing is low at the moment. It is worth looking at this properly.
band.who-5.low: Your wellbeing is on the low side. This is a useful thing to track over the coming weeks.
band.who-5.adequate: Your general wellbeing looks reasonable at the moment.
band.audit-c.low: Your answers do not suggest drinking is adding to the picture.
band.audit-c.risky: Your drinking is at a level where including some substance-aware options makes sense.
band.pc-ptsd-5.negative: This screen did not raise anything to follow up.
band.pc-ptsd-5.positive: A past event still seems to be affecting you. Someone trained in trauma-informed care is likely to be a better fit.
rung.self-help.label: Self-help and prevention

rung.peer-community.label: Peer and community support

rung.group-therapy.label: Group therapy

rung.short-term-individual.label: Short-term individual therapy

rung.kela-rehabilitative.label: Kela rehabilitative psychotherapy
rung.kela-rehabilitative.description: Long-term subsidised psychotherapy. Requires three months of treatment contact and a psychiatrist's statement.

crisis.body: One of your answers suggests you may be having thoughts of harming yourself. That takes courage to say, even to a screen. Please talk to a person — these lines are free, confidential, and answered by trained people.
crisis.alwaysAvailable: Need to talk to someone now?
crisis.notDiagnosis: Reitti is not an emergency service and cannot contact anyone on your behalf.
